label: early copy steps (recall 1-2) when the current or next output is h/2/i/r/u/3
predicate: (phase == 2) & (recall_idx <= 2) & (isin(out_tok, [tok("h"), tok("2"), tok("i"), tok("r"), tok("u"), tok("3")]) | isin(next_out, [tok("h"), tok("2"), tok("i"), tok("r"), tok("u"), tok("3")]))
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, never during the original tokens or on <DEL>. Nearly all activation mass falls on recall_idx 1 (74%, the step right after <DEL>, which re-reads orig(0)) and recall_idx 2 (24%). It almost never fires at recall_idx 0 or 4 and later. Within that window, rate and magnitude depend on which token is being output now or next: h is strongest (lift 9x; every top example has orig(1)=h, often followed by h or 2), then 2, i, r, 3, u. The input token itself hardly matters. Restricting to recall 1-2 with out_tok or next_out in {h,2,i,r,u,3} captures about 91% of mass at roughly 41% precision. It also fires weakly on early copy steps with other outputs, so the token preference is graded rather than strict. Rate drops for L >= 7.
